paper.title_en: Archival X-Ray Observations of the Eclipsing Algol-type Binary TV~Cassiopeiae
paper.abstract_en: TV~Cassiopeiae (TV~Cas) is an eclipsing Algol-type binary with a B9\,V primary and an evolved late-type secondary in a 1.81-day orbit. We examine six serendipitous Chandra and two XMM-Newton observations spanning 2003--2012. The supplied Chandra spectra show thermal plasma near 1~keV and sub-solar fitted abundances, with an additional hotter component in one observation. EPIC-pn fits improve substantially with two temperatures: approximately 0.74/1.39~keV in 2003 and 0.87/2.16~keV in 2012. At 240~pc their nominal intrinsic 0.3--8~keV luminosities are $7.1\times10^{30}$ and $1.2\times10^{31}$~erg~s$^{-1}$, but residual structure, particularly in 2012, and response-calibration uncertainties limit physical interpretation. A prominent flare-like event occurs in Chandra ObsID 08458 (2006-11-04). The longest observation carried out in 2012 pn light curve spans approximately 82\% of an orbit and shows no conspicuous deep eclipse at the predicted secondary conjunction. An exploratory multi-epoch fold contains apparent troughs, but heterogeneous responses, intrinsic variability, and ephemeris uncertainty prevent a unique orbital interpretation. Thermal spectra and flare-like behavior favor a magnetically active secondary corona. The available products do not securely determine a coronal scale height, an orbital modulation amplitude, elemental abundance changes, or the fractional contributions of other unresolved emitters.
